candidate_relations.reason: The CT findings (abnormal SMA-SMV relationship with vein to the left of artery, clustered small-bowel loops with mesenteric congestion, absent duodenum in normal position, low transverse colon) are classic for intestinal malrotation with a right paraduodenal hernia. While malrotation is the underlying anatomical substrate, the specific diagnosis is right paraduodenal hernia—not midgut volvulus. There is no CT evidence of volvulus (no whirlpool sign, no bowel ischemia, no closed-loop obstruction). Adding 'midgut volvulus' asserts an incompatible complication/state not supported by the record, and the candidate omits the paraduodenal hernia entirely.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Malrotation is present (SMA-SMV inversion, abnormal bowel positioning) but midgut volvulus is not supported; the reference diagnosis is right paraduodenal hernia, a distinct entity

case_quality_flags: SMA-SMV inversion (vein left of artery) is a recognized feature of right paraduodenal hernia/malrotation; absence of ischemia and whirlpool sign argues against concurrent volvulus
